title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase (3.7%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $3.97 saw sales 15-38% below baseline. No prior price increase at this level. Noise-adjusted effect not available. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited evidence.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 124.1. No event or promotion in target week. Price increase to $3.97 (+3.7%) is the only driver. Recent price spikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show sales dropped to 106 and 75 vs baseline (124.1), implying a ~20-38% sales drop at this price. The noise-adjusted effect of past price increases is not available, but two observed drops at similar price points suggest a downward effect. Heatwave (38°C) may boost snack demand, but no historical evidence links heat to sales. No past heatwave weeks with sales data. Use conservative shrinkage: 3.7% price increase → ~15% demand drop, shrunk toward 1.0 due to thin evidence. Final median adjusted down. Spreads unchanged: baseline uncertainty is calibrated.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 124.1 | 5%-95%: 77.2 - 200.6 | 10%-90%: 88.7 - 170.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
